_comment: The App-permission LEDGER (spec-github-core-app-permissions.md). Every key GitHub's OpenAPI description enumerates (github_openapi_extract.json → app_permissions, refreshed by scripts/refresh_openapi_extract.py) must appear here in exactly one state: requested (derived from a manifest source — the ONLY way into the App), exploratory (granted on the installed App without a source; must gain one or be dropped — `until` names the resolver), recommended (read; add when its consuming source lands), deferred (a real need behind a feature not on the fence), declined (never, with the reason), not_applicable (write-only, user-to-server, enterprise). No entry may request write. A key GitHub adds is UNCLASSIFIED and fails tests/test_app_permission_ledger.py — that is the 'have they added permissions we should consider' check, made mechanical. Hand-maintained; the test enforces completeness and consistency with the manifest. Keys GitHub exposes in the UI but omits from the OpenAPI schema (observed 2026-09-02: repository_advisories) carry `catalogue_absent` with the evidence; the verify_app skill diffs the LIVE App's permissions against this ledger, which is the second drift source.

actions.why: Workflows, runs, jobs, caches, artifacts — the execution layer and what it uploaded.

administration.why: Rulesets and repository runners — the gate and where jobs run.

artifact_metadata.why: Build artifact metadata records — a new surface whose contents must be understood before it is requested.

attestations.why: Artifact attestations (SLSA provenance): the `attested` property on BUILDS_PACKAGE_VERSION, whose absence is the finding.

checks.why: Check runs and suites: what the gate required and what answered — the required-checks half of why-isn't-this-merging. Requested 2026-09-08 (github-core#82): the head commit's `statusCheckRollup` CheckRun contexts on every collected pull request.

contents.why: Workflow YAML, refs, and releases (#31). Also the `git/ref` and `git/tags` lookups that resolve an out-of-scope action's tag or branch to its commit (req-github-core-actions-used-6).

custom_properties_for_organizations.why: The organisation's custom-property VALUES — the UI's 'Custom properties' control under Organization permissions maps to this key (observed on the App 2026-09-02 after George granted it). Rulesets target repositories by property; the values are what resolves which rulesets apply.

dependabot_secrets.why: Dependabot secret names. A SEPARATE store from Actions secrets: a workflow's `${{ secrets.X }}` never reads one, so it cannot resolve an Actions reference and the reference join does not need it. Its own value is the Dependabot side of the same question — which credentials the update bot holds — and that needs a source of its own.

deployments.why: Deployments and their statuses: what shipped where — the left edge of the machinery.

environments.why: Environment protection rules, reviewers and deployment branch policy — the fields the environment node held as null until req-github-core-settings-4 read them from the REST environment. Read-only: who approves a deployment and which branches may deploy.

issues.why: Not a pipeline fact; waiting-on-me may want it later.

members.why: Teams and members: bypass actors and CODEOWNERS resolve to teams; who-owns-this needs it.
members.until: a who-owns-this / bypass-actor source consumes it (git-serious spec who-owns-this; github-core #39)

merge_queues.why: Merge queue state: the other half of why-isn't-this-merging.

metadata.why: Mandatory for any App; repository listing and identity.

organization_administration.why: App installations on the organisation — the robots with commit rights — and, since req-github-core-settings, the organization's policy block and Actions policy: 2FA requirement, default repository permission, member privileges, security defaults for new repositories, which actions workflows may use.

organization_copilot_seat_management.why: Seat management is licensing, not the pipeline; the Copilot agents' runs are already visible as dynamic workflows.

organization_custom_properties.why: Custom-property DEFINITIONS and the organization's per-repository VALUES (`/orgs/{org}/properties/schema` and `/orgs/{org}/properties/values` both read at this key per GitHub's endpoint docs; `custom_properties_for_organizations` and `repository_custom_properties` are the org-level and repository-level value surfaces, not needed by these two sources). A definition explains a property a repository has not set yet — the difference between 'unset' and 'no such property'. Granted read 2026-09-02; requested 2026-09-08 by req-github-core-custom-properties.

organization_custom_roles.why: Custom repository roles: bypass actors are often role ids (RepositoryRole 5 in the #11 probe) — resolve them to names.

organization_events.why: The organisation activity stream: below Enterprise there is no audit log, and this is the nearest thing to 'what changed since last week'.

organization_external_properties_for_rep.why: Management of external custom properties for repositories in an organization — new in GitHub's OpenAPI description (appeared when the extract was refreshed 2026-10-13 for github-core#68); a custom-properties surface whose contents have not been assessed. Classified here only because the refresh made it unclassified.

organization_hooks.why: Organisation webhooks, same reasoning at the org level.

organization_packages.why: Packages and their versions under the account (#31). Declared because the collector asks GitHub for them, and recorded as a gap: organisation-scoped packages, including ghcr images not linked to a repository. The catalogue lists it, but GitHub's App-settings UI exposes no organisation-level packages permission (observed 2026-09-02): repository `packages: read` on an all-repositories installation reaches packages linked to a repository, and an unlinked package stays NOT OBSERVABLE until GitHub exposes this key — record the gap, do not render it as none. Same measurement applies: no UI control, and the org container listing is closed to Apps regardless.

organization_personal_access_token_reque.why: Pending PAT requests, the pair to the grants above.

organization_personal_access_tokens.why: Fine-grained PAT grants on the organisation — an App-only surface, the second half of 'who can change our code'.
organization_personal_access_tokens.until: a PAT-grants source lands (self-describing-credential spec, github-core #15)

organization_plan.why: The plan tier decides which surfaces can exist at all (audit log, some ruleset features): the difference between 'none' and 'not observable on this plan'.

organization_secrets.why: Organisation secret NAMES and each one's sharing `visibility` — names only, same names-never-values fact as the repository key. Not optional alongside it: the estate's most-shared referenced names live at organisation scope and in no repository, so without this key a dozen workflows would be reported as naming secrets that do not exist. `visibility` is the blast-radius field — how many repositories a single credential reaches.

organization_self_hosted_runners.why: Organisation-level self-hosted runners — where jobs execute; repository runners already come via administration.

packages.why: GitHub Packages published from the pipeline — the outputs column (decided 2026-09-02). MEASURED 2026-09-02 with `packages: read` granted and accepted (installation token, 29 permissions): `GET /orgs/{org}/packages?package_type=container` still answers 400 'Invalid argument' while ghcr images exist (npm/docker list 200 empty); `GET /orgs/{org}/packages/container/{name}/versions` answers 200 by name. Enumeration of container packages is closed to Apps; detail by known name is open. The collector must record enumeration as NOT OBSERVABLE and may resolve names it can derive (publish workflows, envelope hints) — never render the 400 as 'no packages'.

pages.why: Pages builds and configuration: a deployment output for static-site repositories (samsite-shaped).

profile.why: User-to-server; the App observes an organisation and never acts as a user.

pull_requests.why: Pull requests, reviews, approvals: the admission gate's subject; waiting-on-me and why-isn't-this-merging. Requested 2026-09-08 by req-github-core-pull-requests (github-core#82): the config-layer `pullRequests` field.

repository_advisories.catalogue_absent: Present in GitHub's App-settings UI as 'Repository security advisories' and on the App (observed via GET /app, 2026-09-02); ABSENT from components.schemas.app-permissions in the OpenAPI description. The catalogue is incomplete; the live App is the second source.
repository_advisories.why: Repository security advisories and private vulnerability reports — the intake side of processing a security incident, alongside Dependabot and secret-scanning alerts. Added by George 2026-09-02; kept.

repository_custom_properties.why: Rulesets target repositories by custom property; without the values, which rulesets apply cannot be resolved.

repository_hooks.why: Repository webhooks: outbound integrations are third parties past the event horizon, and a webhook to the wrong host is a finding.

repository_projects.why: Project boards are planning, not the pipeline.

secret_scanning_alerts.why: Secret-scanning alerts: the secret-in-code-detection feature (table stakes, security axis). Sensitive read.

secrets.why: Lists secret NAMES only, never values — GitHub's API cannot return a value and TAP stores none. Resolves `${{ secrets.X }}` references to the secret that exists (REFERENCES_SECRET), which is what surfaces a reference pointing at nothing and a credential nothing consumes. Covers both repository and environment secrets. Requested 2026-09-10 (github-core#104), as the deferred entry it replaces said it should be.

security_events.why: Code-scanning alerts: the OUTPUT of the CodeQL dynamic workflow, and the alert surface of the security axis. Sensitive read — say so in the App's review table. Requested 2026-09-09 (github-core#89): the alert and analysis listings per repository, each alert minted as a compliance_core finding.

single_file.why: An alternative to contents for a single path; contents is already held.

statuses.why: Commit statuses: the older check API that Codacy, Sonar and other third parties still post; required checks can be statuses. Requested 2026-09-08 (github-core#82): the StatusContext half of the same rollup.

vulnerability_alerts.why: Dependabot alerts on the repositories the pipeline builds from. github_core's to request (decided 2026-09-02): security incidents are processed here, not held until a supply-chain product exists — the identity of the vulnerable package may later be a supply_chain_core purl, but the alert is a GitHub fact on a GitHub repository. Requested 2026-10-13 (github-core#68): the alert listing per repository, each alert minted as a compliance_core finding. Sensitive read — say so in the App's review table.
